# A struct crossing into JavaScript carries the property names the module
# declared, not the SNGL names the importer derived from them.
#
# The importer lowers a TypeScript property's leading capital to reach a SNGL
# field name, so a PascalCase property is spelled two ways. Writing an argument
# by the SNGL spelling hands the function an object it cannot read: every
# property is undefined, the sum is NaN, and NaN has no SNGL form — so the key
# fails and the build stops rather than folding a wrong number. Reading one by
# the SNGL spelling is the same mistake in the other direction, and it survives
# into the page because nothing at build time looks at it.
[!node] skip
env SNGL_CONSTEVAL_CACHE=$WORK/evalcache

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

grep '30' out/index.html
grep '\.X' out/index.html
! grep '\.x\b' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"
import lib "js://./lib"

const total = lib.sum(lib.Point{x = 10.0, y = 20.0})

component main {
    text(value=string(total))
    var p = lib.origin()
    text(value=string(p.x))
}
-- lib/index.ts --
export interface Point {
    X: number;
    Y: number;
}

/** @sngl-pure */
export function sum(p: Point): number {
    return p.X + p.Y;
}

export function origin(): Point {
    return { X: 3, Y: 4 };
}
